title: Tarsila do Amaral's birth chart
metaDescription: Tarsila do Amaral's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 9.1° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Across the ten placements whose signs are settled, cardinal leads with four. The four cardinal signs sit at the solstices and equinoxes — the scheme’s ignition points, and this chart is weighted to them.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 9.1° Virgo. That falls in the first decan, 0°–10°, sub-ruled by Mercury in the classical scheme — an earth sign read through a mutable season.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Leo (21.0°), Venus in Leo (15.6°), Mars in Scorpio (6.8°): a mind that decides at speaking speed, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate, drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Jupiter to Uranus, a conjunction with 2.0° of slack. Two bodies in the same degree are not read as neighbours but as a merger: whatever one wants, the other is already funding. Behind it, Uranus trine Pluto at 2.2°, and the Sun sextile Mars at 2.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. Mars in Scorpio at 6.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Cancer at 19.1° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements air 4, earth 2, fire 2, water 2; modalities cardinal 4, fixed 4, mutable 2. Air runs on comparison and connection — the pattern noticed first, the feeling filed second. Neptune was retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Libra for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.4° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 22.2°.
